text:
maya: Quick accessibility pass on the Model Details panel — ran through keyboard nav + VoiceOver. Found a few things: heading doesn't receive focus, example prompts have low contrast, and the version selector isn't announced correctly. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.internal/notes/mdl-panel.png

sam: Thanks Maya — can you paste the VoiceOver log or a short repro? Which OS/browser?

maya: macOS 12.6, Safari 16, VoiceOver on. Repro steps: Tab into the panel, press VO+Right to browse — the model title isn't surfaced as a heading in the rotor. Example cards read as static text, contrast measured ~3.8:1 (#8a8a8a on #f7f7f7). Version combobox announces as "button" but doesn't read selected value.

alex: For headings we should avoid tabindex hacks — best to use a semantic <h2> in the markup so screen readers pick it up in the rotor. For contrast, moving to #626262 should hit 4.5:1 for body text on that bg.

sam: I'll take the markup fixes. Quick question — are example prompts interactive? Right now they're divs.

maya: They copy to clipboard on click and expand to show details, so they should be buttons. Also the keyboard focus style is very subtle: current CSS uses `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(45,140,255,0.15)` which is almost invisible on light cards.

tina: a11y-bot scan results: contrast failures -> example-card-text (3.79), truncated-label (2.6). Missing attributes: version-selector missing `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, model-meta region missing `aria-label`.

jeff: Prioritize fixes: 1) keyboard order & semantic controls for examples (copy/expand), 2) make version selector announce selected value, 3) update color tokens. Can we get a small design + implementation plan?

alex: Plan: (a) swap example divs -> `<button class="example-card" aria-expanded="false">` (b) set `--card-text: #3a3a3a` for examples (c) change focus to `outline: 2px solid #2d8cff` instead of faint shadow. I'll mock in Figma and attach.

sam: Opening PR with semantic headings + div->button swap + color token update. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1423 — needs UX and a11y review.

maya: Reviewing PR now. Two quick nits: buttons with icon-only content need `aria-label`; and when an example expands, `aria-expanded` toggles but focus stays on trigger — screen reader users often expect focus to move into the expanded region.

tina: Recommendation: either move focus to the first focusable element inside the expansion, or keep focus but ensure `aria-controls` points to the expanded region id and the region has `role="region"` + accessible name.

jeff: Sounds good. Can we do a quick 15m handoff after merge to validate VoiceOver?

alex: Scheduled a 15m sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. I'll add a QA checklist to the PR describing VoiceOver steps, keyboard tab order, and contrast checks.

maya: LGTM after the small aria tweaks. :thumbsup: I'll re-run VoiceOver after changes are deployed to staging.

sam: Merged to branch and deploying to staging now — tagging @maya for post-deploy verification.

a11y-bot: Staging scan (post-PR): contrast passes for updated tokens, navigation improvements detected. Remaining low-level warning: "expanded region lacks accessible name" (recommend add `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).

maya: Thanks — will check the staging page once deploy finishes and follow up with a short note in the PR about the remaining label.

sam: Deploy finished. Staging URL: https://staging.redwood.dev/models/xyz. Maya, if you can confirm the rotor and VoiceOver announces, we'll ship.

maya: Verified: rotor now shows model title, example buttons are announced as buttons and read labels, version selector reads selected value. Found one last nit: when you open an example the expanded panel isn't announced with a live region — adding `aria-live="polite"` to the region would help non-visual users notice dynamic content changes.

alex: Will add `aria-live="polite"` to the expansion container and include `aria-label` for the region title. Thanks for the thorough pass!

tina: Final automated check queued — will post results in PR comments.

jeff: Excellent. Great cross-team turnaround on a small accessibility regression.
